1.title: The Song of the Bow
1.text: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan was called 'the Bow' and was taught to the children of Judah. From it comes the phrase 'How are the mighty fallen!'

1.question: Who brought David the news of Saul's death?
options: An Amalekite who had fled the battle
A young soldier from Saul's own guard
A messenger who had been sent by Abner
A wounded soldier from Gilboa

1.question: What did the Amalekite claim, hoping for David's favor?
options: That he himself had killed Saul
That he had saved Jonathan
That he had beaten the Philistines
That he was Saul's kinsman

1.question: What did David do with the man who boasted of killing the Lord's anointed?
options: He had him put to death
He appointed him as a captain
He pardoned him and sent him away
He exiled him from the kingdom

1.question: What did David compose on learning of Saul and Jonathan's deaths?
options: A lament for them
A victory song
A law
A letter to Abner

1.question: What famous phrase marks David's lament?
options: 'How are the mighty fallen!'
'Blessed be the name of the Lord'
'The Lord is my strength and song'
'I will fear no evil at all'

1.question: For whom did David express deep friendship in the lament?
options: Jonathan
Abner
Saul
Joab

2.title: Hebron, the first capital
2.text: David reigned over Judah at Hebron for seven and a half years before becoming king over all Israel and moving the capital to Jerusalem.

2.question: Where was David anointed king over Judah?
options: Hebron
Jerusalem
Beth-lehem
Shiloh

2.question: Whom did Abner make king over Israel, David's rival?
options: Ish-bosheth, Saul's son
Malchishua, Saul's own son
Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son
Joab, David's own nephew

2.question: What happened by the pool of Gibeon?
options: A battle between David's men and Ish-bosheth's
A peace treaty signed between David and Saul's house
A solemn coronation of David as new king over all Israel
A great sacrifice offered to the Lord by Abner

2.question: Whom did Abner kill in the pursuit, Joab's brother?
options: Asahel
Abishai
Amasa
Uriah

2.question: What did Abner ask Joab at the end of the day of fighting?
options: That the slaughter between brothers cease
That he surrender immediately to the army
That he hand over David to the sons of Benjamin
That they fight until nightfall came

2.question: Who suffered far more casualties in that battle?
options: Abner's men (Israel)
David's men, from Judah
The Philistines gathered at Aphek
The Ammonites besieged at Rabbah

2.question: How many of David's men died, besides Asahel?
options: Nineteen
Three hundred
A thousand
Seventy

3.title: A long war
3.text: The war between the house of David and the house of Saul lasted a long time; little by little David grew stronger and Saul's house weaker.

3.question: At the chapter's start, how stood the war between the two houses?
options: David grew stronger and Saul's house weaker
It was even, with no clear advantage to either side
Saul's house was winning and David losing ground
It was already over with Saul's total victory

3.question: What led Abner to turn to David's side?
options: A quarrel with Ish-bosheth
A secret order from Samuel
A dream revealed by an angel
The sudden death of Joab

3.question: What condition did David require of Abner for a covenant?
options: That he bring Michal back to him
That he hand over much gold and silver
That he give him half of the whole kingdom
That he bring Ish-bosheth's head

3.question: What did Abner go to do among the tribes of Israel?
options: Persuade them to accept David as king
Gather a great army against King David
Flee with them to the kingdom of the Philistines
Crown himself king in front of them

3.question: What did Joab think of the peace Abner made with David?
options: He distrusted it and accused him of spying
He fully approved of the agreement that was made
He completely ignored the peace proposal offered
He celebrated with the entire army

3.question: How did Joab kill Abner?
options: Treacherously, at the gate of Hebron, avenging Asahel
In fair battle, before the eyes of his whole gathered army
By the very direct order of King David himself, in secret
With poison slowly placed into his wine cup

3.question: How did David react to Abner's death?
options: He mourned and fasted, showing he had not ordered it
He rewarded Joab publicly before all of his gathered people
He ignored the matter and continued the feast as usual
He fled Hebron for fear of sudden reprisals

3.question: What did the people understand from David's mourning for Abner?
options: That the king was not guilty of the death
That David was far too weak to govern properly
That Joab was completely innocent of all guilt
That the war would soon continue on

4.title: David builds on no man's blood
4.text: For the third time David punishes those who kill to please him (the Amalekite, and now Ish-bosheth's murderers): his kingdom is not built on treachery.

4.question: How was Ish-bosheth after Abner's death?
options: He grew weak, and Israel was troubled
He grew strong and gathered a great army
He made an alliance with the Philistines
He fled to Gath with his family

4.question: What did two captains do to Ish-bosheth?
options: They killed him in his sleep and brought his head to David
They crowned him king over all Israel and Judah before the people
They imprisoned him and handed him over to the Philistines as a captive
They defended him bravely against all his enemies

4.question: What did David do to Ish-bosheth's murderers?
options: He had them executed
He rewarded them
He made them captains
He freed them

5.title: The city of David
5.text: By capturing the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites, David made Jerusalem his capital; it came to be called 'the city of David.'

5.question: What did all the tribes of Israel do with David at Hebron?
options: They anointed him king over all Israel
They drove him out of the throne and exiled him from Israel
They demanded tribute in the name of the whole people
They crowned Ish-bosheth once more over Israel

5.question: What city did David capture and make his capital?
options: Jerusalem (the stronghold of Zion)
Hebron, where he first reigned over Judah
Gath, a city of the Philistines by the sea
Shiloh, where the ark had been kept

5.question: Why did David grow greater and greater?
options: Because the Lord of hosts was with him
Because of his huge army and great wealth
Because of an alliance with Egypt and Tyre
Because of his own strength and wisdom

5.question: Who helped David build his palace?
options: Hiram, king of Tyre
The ancient pharaoh of Egypt
The princes of the Philistines
Solomon, his son

5.question: What did David do before attacking the Philistines?
options: He inquired of the Lord
He gathered war chariots
He fled into the mountains
He sought a truce with the Philistines

5.question: What sign did God give David to attack, in the tops of the mulberry trees?
options: A sound of marching in the treetops
A loud thunderclap from atop the mountains
A shining bright star pointing the way
A pillar of fire descending from the sky

6.title: The ark is no common object
6.text: The Law required that only the Levites carry the ark, with poles. Transporting it on a new cart, like the Philistines, cost Uzzah his life.

6.question: What did David want to bring to Jerusalem?
options: The ark of God
Saul's throne
The tabernacle
The bronze altar

6.question: What happened to Uzzah when he put out his hand to the ark?
options: He was struck dead by God on the spot
He was blessed and rewarded richly by God
He went blind and lost all his strength
Nothing bad happened to him at all

6.question: Where did the ark stay three months, blessing the house?
options: In the house of Obed-edom
In David's royal palace in Jerusalem
In Gibeon, beside the ancient altar
In Shiloh, in the house of the Lord

6.question: What did David do as he brought the ark, full of joy?
options: He danced before the Lord with all his might
He kept complete silence, watching everything with respect
He offered himself as a new priest to serve at the altar
He hid himself behind the tent out of shame

6.question: Why did Michal despise David?
options: For dancing humbly before the people
For losing the battle against the Philistines
For building the temple without consulting the priests
For fasting instead of offering sacrifices

7.title: The Davidic covenant
7.text: The promise of a throne established forever points to Jesus Christ, the 'Son of David,' whose kingdom will have no end (see Luke 1).

7.question: What did David want to build for the Lord?
options: A temple (a house) for the ark
A grand cedar palace for himself
A fortress to guard his treasures
A monument to his own victory

7.question: What did God answer David through the prophet Nathan?
options: That David would not build the house, but God would make David a 'house' (dynasty)
That David should gather the elders of Israel to consecrate a new altar to the Lord
That David hand over the kingdom to his son before setting out for war against the Philistines
That David abdicate the throne in favor of his older brother, Adonijah

7.question: Who would build the temple, according to the promise?
options: A son of David
David himself
Nathan
Solomon and Saul together

7.question: What everlasting promise did God make to David's house?
options: That his throne would be established forever
That he would reign over all the nations of the earth
That he would never again have enemies around him
That his sons would be priests

7.question: What did David do on hearing God's promise?
options: He prayed in gratitude before the Lord
He built a stone altar at the military camp
He gathered the elders to announce the prophecy
He sent gifts to the Israelite priests

7.question: What did David acknowledge about Israel in his prayer?
options: That God had redeemed it from Egypt as his own people
That it was the mightiest nation among all the peoples of the earth
That he deserved to be exalted above all the neighboring kings
That it no longer needed priests or laws

7.question: Concerning what did David ask that God's word be fulfilled?
options: Concerning his house, forever
Concerning the victory over the Philistines
Concerning the building of a greater temple
Concerning Saul's kingdom

8.title: The kingdom's peak
8.text: The chapter lists David's officials (Joab over the army, etc.) and shows the kingdom at its greatest extent, under 'judgment and justice.'

8.question: What does chapter 8 summarize about David?
options: His victories over neighboring peoples
The building of the great temple in Jerusalem
His peace treaty with the neighboring kings
His serious illness late in life

8.question: What did David do with the silver and gold taken in war?
options: He dedicated it to the Lord
He stored it in his palace
He distributed it among his soldiers
He melted it into idols

8.question: How did David reign over all Israel?
options: With judgment and justice for all the people
By the counsel of the priests alone
Following the customs of the neighboring peoples
With an iron hand and much oppression

9.title: Loyalty that keeps the promise
9.text: David sought someone of Saul's house to bless — not out of interest, but to keep the covenant of friendship he had made with Jonathan.

9.question: For whose sake did David want to show kindness to Saul's house?
options: Jonathan
Abner
Samuel
Ish-bosheth

9.question: Who was Mephibosheth, whom David welcomed?
options: Jonathan's son, lame in his feet
Absalom's son, a renowned warrior
Ziba's servant, in charge of the lands
Abigail's nephew, David's kin

9.question: What did David grant Mephibosheth?
options: Saul's lands and a place at his table, like a king's son
An entire army to reconquer his father's lands
The whole throne of Israel, because of his late father Jonathan
Only gold and silver, with no lands or place at the table

10.title: An insult that sparked war
10.text: Shaving off half the beard and cutting the messengers' garments was a severe humiliation; it was the spark of war between Israel and Ammon.

10.question: Why did David send messengers to the king of Ammon?
options: To comfort him over his father's death
To demand tribute for the previous king's death
To negotiate a military alliance against the Philistines
To spy on the city of Rabbah secretly

10.question: How did Hanun treat David's messengers?
options: He humiliated them, shaving their beards and cutting their garments
He welcomed them with honors and invited them to a grand royal banquet
He ordered them executed publicly in the middle of the city of Rabbah
He had them arrested and kept under guard in the palace

10.question: What did the Ammonites do, fearing David's reaction?
options: They hired the Syrians to help them
They sent gifts to appease David
They sought refuge in the mountains of Edom
They shut the gates of all their cities

10.question: What was the result of the wars against Ammon and Syria?
options: David defeated them
David was defeated
There was a truce
The Syrians took Jerusalem

11.title: The danger of idleness
11.text: 'At the time when kings go forth to battle,' David stayed in Jerusalem. Idleness and abuse of power led him to adultery and murder.

11.question: What did David do when he saw Bath-sheba, Uriah's wife?
options: He had her brought and committed adultery
He sent her back and never thought of her again
He asked if she was married and gave up seeing her
He sent for her but changed his mind

11.question: Why did Uriah not go home to rest when David summoned him?
options: Out of loyalty — he would not rest while the ark and army were in the field
Because he feared the other soldiers would judge him for leaving the battlefield
Because Joab had ordered him to keep watch at the door of the palace
Because he wanted to surprise David with news from the war

11.question: What did David write in the letter carried by Uriah himself to Joab?
options: To set Uriah at the front of the battle, so he would die
To appoint Uriah commander over all of Joab's forces
To order Uriah to return home and stay with his wife
To ask Joab to give Uriah a generous reward

11.question: How did Uriah die?
options: In battle, abandoned at the front line
By a stray arrow during the army's retreat
In an ambush set by Joab outside the city
Of an illness caught in the camp

11.question: How does the chapter end, after David took Bath-sheba as wife?
options: 'The thing that David had done displeased the Lord'
'David and Bath-sheba lived in peace at the royal palace'
'The people celebrated David's marriage with great joy'
'Joab received honors for his victory'

12.title: David's repentance
12.text: When confronted, David confessed: 'I have sinned against the Lord.' Psalm 51 is traditionally his prayer of repentance; he was forgiven, but the consequences remained.

12.question: What parable did Nathan tell David?
options: The rich man who took the poor man's only lamb
The shepherd who lost one sheep among a hundred
The two brothers who quarreled over their father's inheritance
The sower who scattered seed in the field

12.question: What did Nathan say, applying the parable to David?
options: 'Thou art the man'
'Go in peace'
'The Lord bless thee'
'Arise and walk'

12.question: What consequence did Nathan announce for David's house?
options: That the sword would not depart from it
That his children would be driven from the kingdom forever
That the people would rise up against him in rebellion
That he would lose the priesthood blessing

12.question: What did David say when confronted by Nathan?
options: 'I have sinned against the Lord'
'God will forgive me without punishment'
'It was Bath-sheba who tempted me to sin'
'This is no sin, I am the king'

12.question: How did David react when the sick child died?
options: He arose, washed, and worshiped the Lord
He wept and fasted for seven more days in mourning
He tore his clothes and covered himself with ashes in grief
He refused to leave his room for many days

12.question: What son of David and Bath-sheba was born afterward, loved by the Lord?
options: Solomon
Absalom
Amnon
Adonijah

12.question: What city did Joab take, and David received the king's crown?
options: Rabbah, of the Ammonites
Joppa, of the Philistines
Gibeah, of Benjamin
Shechem, of Ephraim

13.title: The sword in David's house
13.text: From here Nathan's words come true: violence and tragedy strike David's own family, beginning with Amnon and Tamar.

13.question: With whom did Amnon, David's son, become sickly infatuated?
options: Tamar, his half-sister
Maacah, Absalom's mother
Abishag the young Shunammite
Rizpah, daughter of Aiah

13.question: How did Amnon lure Tamar close to him?
options: He feigned illness and asked her to serve him
He claimed to be wounded in battle and asked for her care
He sent a letter pretending to be the king's order
He promised her expensive gifts and jewels

13.question: What did Amnon do to Tamar?
options: He violated her by force
He promised her immediate marriage
He begged forgiveness and sent her to David
He received her with great warmth

13.question: How did Amnon treat Tamar afterward?
options: He came to hate her and sent her away
He kept her in his chambers as a wife
He publicly reconciled with her afterward
He offered her many valuable gifts

13.question: How did Absalom react to what Amnon had done to his sister?
options: He kept silent, but came to hate Amnon
He went to King David and asked that Amnon be punished
He secretly reconciled with Amnon
He drove Amnon from the royal palace

13.question: What did Absalom do two years later, at a sheepshearing feast?
options: He had his servants kill Amnon
He invited all his brothers to a royal feast
He ordered Joab to lead an attack
He asked his father David for forgiveness

13.question: What exaggerated report first reached David?
options: That all his sons had been killed
That Absalom had been crowned king in his place
That Joab had rebelled against the throne
That Tamar had also been killed

13.question: Where did Absalom flee after killing Amnon?
options: To Geshur
To Egypt
To Hebron
To Gath

14.title: Absalom's hair
14.text: Absalom was famed for his beauty and his very heavy head of hair, which he cut once a year — a detail that would play a tragic part in his death.

14.question: Who devised a plan to bring Absalom back from exile?
options: Joab
Nathan
Shimei
Ziba

14.question: Whom did Joab send to David with a parable, to move him?
options: A wise woman of Tekoah
A prophetess of the royal court
A personal servant of David
A priest of the temple

14.question: What did the woman of Tekoah obtain from David?
options: That he allow Absalom's return
That he restore her confiscated lands
That he name her son heir to the throne
That he exempt her from taxes

14.question: What condition did David set in letting Absalom return to Jerusalem?
options: That he would not see the king's face
That he surrender his weapons to the king
That he serve as a slave in the palace
That he never speak with Joab

14.question: What was Absalom especially known for in Israel?
options: His beauty and his thick head of hair
His great wisdom and his sound counsel
His extraordinary strength and his courage
His kindness and generosity

14.question: What did Absalom do to force Joab to receive him?
options: He had Joab's field set on fire
He sent messengers to the king repeatedly
He threatened to reveal royal secrets
He refused to leave his house

15.title: The prayer against Ahithophel
15.text: Ahithophel, a counselor famed for his wisdom, joined Absalom. David prayed: 'O Lord, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness' — and sent Hushai to do it.

15.question: How did Absalom steal the hearts of the people of Israel?
options: By flattering them at the gate and promising them justice
By offering gifts and positions to the leaders of the tribes
By summoning the people to the temple to pray for justice
By sending spies with promises of great riches

15.question: Where did Absalom proclaim himself king, starting the conspiracy?
options: Hebron
Jerusalem
Gibeon
Shiloh

15.question: What did David do on learning of Absalom's revolt?
options: He fled Jerusalem with his followers
He called a council of war in the city
He reinforced the walls and awaited the siege
He negotiated peace with Absalom

15.question: Who insisted on following David, though a foreigner?
options: Ittai the Gittite
Amasa, his nephew
Zadok the high priest
Joab the general

15.question: What did David tell Zadok to do with the ark of God?
options: Carry it back to Jerusalem
Leave it hidden in the wilderness
Keep it in the tabernacle at Gibeon
Entrust it to faithful Levites

15.question: Why did David not take the ark with him?
options: He trusted God would bring him back if it pleased Him
He feared enemies would destroy it during the long flight
He thought the priests should remain inside the temple
He considered it too heavy a burden for the flight

15.question: Whom did David send back to Jerusalem to thwart Ahithophel?
options: Hushai, his friend
Joab, his commander
Abishai, his nephew
Gad, the prophet

16.title: Nathan's word fulfilled
16.text: Ahithophel's counsel for Absalom to take his father's concubines in open sight fulfilled what Nathan had prophesied about the consequences of David's sin.

16.question: What did Ziba bring David, accusing Mephibosheth?
options: Provisions, saying Mephibosheth hoped to regain the kingdom
A secret army, claiming that Absalom would need reinforcements
Saul's gold, saying it would be used to bribe the king's soldiers
A sealed letter accusing Mephibosheth of treason against the king

16.question: Who cursed David and threw stones during the flight?
options: Shimei, of Saul's house
Ahithophel, the traitorous counselor
Joab, the commander of David's army
Ittai, the ever-faithful Gittite

16.question: How did David react to Shimei, who cursed him?
options: He bore it, saying perhaps the Lord had allowed it
He ordered Abishai to arrest him at once for his great insolence
He mocked him openly, saying his words meant nothing at all
He pretended not to hear and quickened his pace in total silence

16.question: What counsel did Ahithophel give Absalom to defy David?
options: To take publicly the concubines David had left
To gather the whole army at once and attack David without delay
To crown Absalom before all the people gathered in Jerusalem
To send messengers to negotiate peace with David

17.title: Providence over the counsel
17.text: The text says 'the Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel' — Absalom preferred Hushai's counsel, and it led him to ruin.

17.question: What counsel did Ahithophel give Absalom about David?
options: To pursue him at once, that very night
To wait until gathering twelve thousand men again at Gilgal
To make an immediate alliance with the Philistines against David
To send letters threatening the elders of Israel

17.question: What contrary counsel did Hushai give?
options: To wait and gather all Israel first
To pursue David immediately with twelve thousand men
To surround the city where David was hiding
To send spies to discover his whereabouts

17.question: Which counsel did Absalom end up following, to his ruin?
options: Hushai's
Ahithophel's
The priests'
Joab's

17.question: How was David warned to flee beyond the Jordan?
options: By messengers sent by the priests
By a dream revealed to Nathan the prophet
By a young man who saw it and told Absalom
By a vision David had at night

17.question: What did Ahithophel do when his counsel was rejected?
options: He hanged himself
He fled to Geshur
He begged David's pardon
He attacked Absalom

17.question: Who sustained David with provisions at Mahanaim?
options: Loyal allies, like Barzillai
Foreign merchants who came from beyond the Jordan
Soldiers secretly sent by Absalom
Priests who came from Jerusalem

18.title: 'O my son Absalom!'
18.text: Despite his son's betrayal, David wept bitterly: 'would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son!' — one of the Bible's most moving laments.

18.question: What order did David give the captains about Absalom before the battle?
options: To deal gently with the young man
To capture him alive and bring him in chains
To have the captains execute him immediately
To kill him without delay

18.question: Where was the decisive battle against Absalom fought?
options: In the wood of Ephraim
In the fields of Gilgal
By the walls of Mahanaim
Close to Jerusalem

18.question: How was Absalom caught, defenseless?
options: By his head (hair) in an oak
By his robe caught on an olive tree's branches
By his feet tangled in a tree's roots
Caught by his garment in a thornbush

18.question: Who killed Absalom, against David's order?
options: Joab
Abishai
Ittai
Hushai

18.question: Who ran to bring David news of the battle?
options: Ahimaaz and the Cushite
Zadok and Ahimaaz
Abiathar and the Cushite
One of Joab's servants

18.question: How did David react on learning of Absalom's death?
options: He wept bitterly for his son
He refused to receive the victorious army
He ordered public mourning for the people
He blamed Joab for his son's death

19.title: Joab's bluntness
19.text: Joab, though he had disobeyed by killing Absalom, rebuked David sharply: the king's excessive mourning was shaming the army that had saved him.

19.question: What did the army feel because of David's grief?
options: They were ashamed of the victory, as if they had lost
Feared that David would banish them from the kingdom in revenge
Decided to abandon Jerusalem and return to their tents
Asked that Joab take command of the army

19.question: What did Joab demand of David?
options: That he rise and speak to the people, or be abandoned
That he name Amasa the new commander of the army at once
That he gather the elders of Judah to swear loyalty to him
That he reward the soldiers for their victory

19.question: What were the tribes debating after Absalom's defeat?
options: Bringing David back as king
Naming Amasa as the new ruler
Sending messengers to calm Israel
Making an alliance with the Philistines

19.question: What did David do with Shimei, who had cursed him?
options: He pardoned him and swore not to kill him
Ordered that he be held until further notice
Had Abishai execute him on the spot
Demanded that he leave the country

19.question: What did Mephibosheth claim about not following David in the flight?
options: That Ziba had deceived and slandered him
That his servants had abandoned him in the flight
That he had been kept from leaving by his servants
That he was mourning for his father

19.question: How did Mephibosheth react when David divided the lands between him and Ziba?
options: He said Ziba could take it all, glad the king returned in peace
He insisted on keeping his own portion of land, refusing to yield anything to Ziba
He accused Ziba again before the king and demanded all the lands be returned to him
He remained silent and left everything in the king's hands

19.question: Who was Barzillai, who had helped David at Mahanaim?
options: An old and wealthy Gileadite
A Levite of the tribe of Judah
A commander of Israel's army
A merchant from Jerusalem

19.question: What did Barzillai answer to David's invitation to live at court?
options: He declined, being very old, and named another in his place
He accepted, but asked to return soon to his own hometown
He asked to bring along his whole family and all his servants
He declined for fear of the king's remaining enemies

19.question: What conflict arose on the king's return to Jerusalem?
options: A dispute between Judah and Israel over who would bring the king
A new armed rebellion led by Sheba, the son of Bichri, against David
A dispute between Joab and Amasa over the command of the army
A clash between the elders of Gilgal and of Judah

20.title: The wise woman of Abel
20.text: For the second time in the book, a 'wise woman' prevents a massacre: she negotiated with Joab, and the city of Abel was spared by handing over the rebel.

20.question: Who led a new revolt, saying 'we have no part in David'?
options: Sheba son of Bichri
Joab son of Zeruiah
Absalom son of David
Shimei son of Gera

20.question: Whom did Joab treacherously kill during the pursuit of Sheba?
options: Amasa
Abishai
Ittai
Barzillai

20.question: Where did Sheba take refuge, being besieged?
options: In the city of Abel
In the city of Hebron
In the fortress of Zelah
On Mount Ephraim

20.question: How was the city of Abel spared?
options: A wise woman negotiated, and they handed over Sheba's head
The city elders surrendered and released Sheba completely unharmed
Joab negotiated peace and Sheba fled to the Berites in secret
The people opened the gates and gave hostages to Joab

20.question: What does the end of the chapter list?
options: David's chief officials
The cities reconquered by Joab
The priests and prophets of the realm
The royal lineages of Israel

21.title: Rizpah's devotion
21.text: Rizpah watched over the bodies of Saul's sons for months, keeping off birds and beasts; her devotion moved David to honorably bury the bones of Saul and Jonathan.

21.question: What was the cause of the three-year famine in David's time?
options: Saul's bloodguilt against the Gibeonites
The people's refusal to pay tithes at the Lord's temple
The breaking of David's covenant with the neighboring Philistines
A curse pronounced by Saul over the land of Israel

21.question: What did the Gibeonites ask as restitution?
options: The handing over of Saul's descendants
Double restitution for everything that was stolen
The building of an altar near Mount Gibeah
The return of the captured lands

21.question: What did Rizpah do by the bodies of Saul's sons?
options: She watched over them, keeping off birds and beasts
She buried them secretly in a nearby cave outside the city
She publicly accused David before the people and the king
She sought help from the Gibeonites in vain

21.question: What does the chapter recount about the wars with the Philistines?
options: The killing of giants, kinsmen of Goliath
The reconquest of Jerusalem by the Philistines
A lasting truce sealed between the two nations
The final capture of the ark of the covenant

22.title: The song that is Psalm 18
22.text: This song of David is virtually identical to Psalm 18 — a poetic summary of a life marked by danger and the Lord's deliverance.

22.question: What is 2 Samuel chapter 22?
options: A song of David praising the Lord for delivering him from enemies
A detailed list of ceremonial laws given to the people of Israel
A complete genealogy of the twelve tribes descended from Jacob
A prophecy of judgment against the neighboring nations of Israel

22.question: What images does David use for God at the start of the song?
options: Rock, fortress and deliverer
Shepherd, lamb and high priest
King, judge and eternal ruler
Father and wise teacher

22.question: To whom does David credit his deliverance?
options: To the Lord, who heard his cry
To his own strength and skill in battle
To his powerful armies well trained for war
To alliances with neighboring kings

22.question: How does the song describe the Lord coming to the rescue?
options: With tremors, smoke and lightning
In a gentle and calm whispering voice from heaven
In a silent procession of angels descending
In a peaceful dream revealed to David

22.question: Why did the Lord deliver David, according to the song?
options: Because he delighted in him
Because David forced him
By chance
Because of the army

22.question: What principle does David declare about God's dealings?
options: That he rewards according to righteousness and integrity
That he completely ignores the evil deeds of all wicked men
That he favors only the rich and powerful of the whole earth
That he changes his mind based on circumstances

22.question: How does God treat the humble and the proud, according to the song?
options: He saves the humble and brings down the haughty
He treats everyone the same without distinction
He always favors the strongest warriors in the battle
He ignores both sides without any distinction

22.question: Who enabled David for battle?
options: God, who girded him with strength
His most experienced military generals
The allied Philistine soldiers nearby
Mere chance and circumstance

22.question: What does David say about his enemies in the song?
options: That he overcame them by the Lord's strength
That he spared them out of great divine mercy
That he fled from them in search of safe refuge
That he allied with neighboring kings

22.question: What does David promise in response to deliverance?
options: To praise and sing to the Lord's name among the nations
To build a magnificent temple for the Lord in Jerusalem
To completely conquer Egypt and all of its vast rich lands
To rest peacefully for the remainder of his days

22.question: To whom does the song credit mercy forever?
options: To the Lord, toward David and his descendants
To the neighboring kings who supported his cause
To the loyal army that always fought by his side
To himself and his own great bravery

23.title: David's mighty men
23.text: Among 'the thirty' mighty men listed is Uriah the Hittite — a silent reminder of David's great sin, even in a chapter that celebrates heroes.

23.question: What are the opening verses of chapter 23?
options: David's last words
David's prayer of repentance
A prophecy about Jerusalem's fall
A list of the kings of Judah

23.question: Who were 'the three' and 'the thirty' named in the chapter?
options: David's chief mighty men (warriors)
The leaders of the twelve tribes who supported David's reign
The priests and Levites responsible for David's tabernacle
The royal counselors appointed by David

23.question: What did one of the mighty men do alone in a field of lentils?
options: He defended it, and the Lord gave a great victory
He abandoned the field and fled with the other soldiers
He gathered the army and attacked the Philistine city
He burned the harvest fields before leaving

23.question: What did three mighty men do for David at Beth-lehem?
options: They broke through the Philistine camp to bring him water from the well
They secretly scaled the walls of Jerusalem to rescue the king's own children
They alone defeated an entire army of Arameans out in the open wilderness
They guided David safely to the mountain stronghold of Adullam

23.question: What did David do with the water three men brought at the risk of their lives?
options: He poured it out to the Lord, refusing to drink it
He shared it among the three mighty men who had brought it
He used it to wash the wounds of the injured soldiers
He saved it to drink after the coming battle

23.question: What deeds of Benaiah does the chapter highlight?
options: He killed a lion in a pit and overcame an Egyptian
He tore down the walls of a Philistine city all by himself
He captured the king of the Ammonites alive in battle
He defeated three giant warriors single-handedly

23.question: What does the end of the chapter list?
options: The names of David's mighty men
The territories conquered by David
The royal decrees issued during his reign
The treasures of the royal treasury

23.question: How many mighty men does David's list total at the end?
options: Thirty-seven
Twelve
Three hundred
Seventy

23.question: Who appears in the roll of mighty men, tied to the story of Bath-sheba?
options: Uriah the Hittite
Elias the Paltite
Zabad, son of Ahlai
Naarai the Arbite

24.title: 'I will not offer that which costs me nothing'
24.text: David refused to receive Araunah's threshingfloor for free: he bought it for the altar. That place, in Jerusalem, would become the mount where Solomon built the temple.

24.question: What sin did David commit, against Joab's counsel?
options: He numbered the people out of pride
He erected altars to foreign idols and gods
He married a Moabite woman against the law
He neglected the yearly sacrifices

24.question: What did David feel after numbering the people?
options: His heart smote him and he acknowledged the sin
Pride at seeing how great his army had truly become
Satisfaction at finally knowing the size of his kingdom
Relief at having finally defeated his enemies

24.question: What choice did the prophet Gad offer David as judgment?
options: Between famine, flight from enemies, or plague
Between the sword, captivity, or a long drought
Between losing the throne, the army, or his family
Between three different plagues of locusts

24.question: What did David choose, and what came upon Israel?
options: To fall into the Lord's hand; a plague came
To flee from his enemies; a great famine came
To face famine; seven years of scarcity came
Nothing; the people remained at peace

24.question: What did David buy to build an altar, where the plague stopped?
options: The threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite
A large field belonging to Boaz near Beth-lehem
The tent belonging to Obed-edom the Gittite
The house of Zadok the high priest
